# Krystian Słowik

> Support & integrations engineer (enterprise tier) at n8n. Kubernetes, integrations, the auth layer, and AI agent pipelines that fail somewhere in the middle — debugged at source. Based in Münster, Germany (CET). Cybersecurity background. Contact: hej@krystianslowik.com.

## About Krystian

Krystian Słowik is a support & integrations engineer at n8n on the enterprise tier: escalated Kubernetes incidents, broken integrations, and AI pipelines that fail somewhere in the middle. He reads the source when the docs lie. His working philosophy: "I break things, fix them, and automate whatever survives. Root cause over vibes — the wrong theory dies when the evidence lands."

As of mid-2026 he is: working self-hosted and cloud n8n deployments (Kubernetes, distributed state, security boundaries, AI agent pipelines); building internal tooling at work (MCP servers, Slack automation, CI/CD), shipping community n8n nodes (n8n-nodes-plainapi), and running a scanning console for his home cluster; and studying cybersecurity part-time. He speaks Polish, English and German.

## Selected work

### End-to-end delivery
End-to-end delivery of an event-driven platform for gigabyte-scale imaging: content-addressed ingest, a native tiler, a domain-specific detection model, and the operational system on top. An instrument pipeline took ~20 minutes per file before anyone could see the contents; he built the chain end to end — versioned content-addressed ingest buffer, a native tiler integration cutting per-file processing to ~1.5 seconds, a RabbitMQ-fed detection service with a custom-trained model, and results flowing into the operational app (lifecycle, billing, reporting) across on-prem GPU and cloud. Outcome: a 20-minute batch step became near-real-time.

### An n8n node, because the platform was missing one
Plain is a support platform built for technical teams; n8n had no node for it. He built and shipped n8n-nodes-plainapi to the community: the full Plain GraphQL surface wrapped in n8n's resource and operation model — 34 operations across threads, customers, companies, emails, notes, labels, users and CSAT, full filter and sort support, a typed credential, strict mode, zero runtime deps. Published on npm, installable from Community Nodes. Outcome: per-workflow GraphQL glue collapsed to one install and a credential.

### Reusable deployment plays, not one-off fixes
Sole author of an enterprise Kubernetes deployment playbook: execution-mode decisions, Helm chart tradeoffs, sizing, security hardening, and a troubleshooting index tied to incidents that actually happened — every engagement codified into a play. Outcome: deployments start from the playbook instead of a blank page.

### Enterprise deployments, debugged at source
Enterprise deployments across EKS and AKS where incidents arrive as symptoms with three plausible causes — TLS handshakes dying between cert validation, a proxy, a WAF and the network layer; licensing state expiring only in multi-instance mode, months apart. Method: run the elimination chain (MTU, SNI, proxy env, DNS, egress) and read the product's source instead of trusting the docs. Outcome: fixes land where the bug actually lives, with evidence customers' infra teams can act on.

### AI pipelines, debugged where they broke
Enterprise agent systems running several model providers at once: tool-call JSON that doesn't match the node's schema, context windows truncating silently mid-chain, retry logic cascading on provider 429s. Traced at the failing layer, with vendor claims verified at source level. Outcome: honest diagnoses — model, prompt, or the infrastructure in between.

## Writing

### Boring is a feature (2026-05-12)
https://krystianslowik.com/writing/boring-is-a-feature/
The best compliment a system can get is silence. On optimising for the absence of surprise — no pages, no war rooms — and the quiet career cost of being the person who keeps the lights on, since "made on-call uneventful" doesn't sparkle on a performance review.

### The postmortem I got wrong (2026-02-03)
https://krystianslowik.com/writing/the-postmortem-i-got-wrong/
The first version had a clean root cause: a bad config value shipped late on a Friday. Tidy, blameless, wrong. The config was a symptom; the real failure was a review process that let a load-bearing change through unquestioned. The honest rewrite, and how he reads his own incident reports since.

### k8s at home, and why it's not a toy (2025-12-18)
https://krystianslowik.com/writing/k8s-at-home/
Three bare-metal Ryzen mini-PCs in a cupboard in Münster: kubeadm, Longhorn, Calico, Cloudflare Tunnel. The only environment where breaking things on purpose is allowed. The homelab is the rehearsal room for production.
